questions.question: In your own words, explain the multiplier effect and why the final change in national income is larger than the initial injection.
questions.expected_answer: The multiplier effect occurs because an initial injection of spending (like government expenditure) becomes income for others, who then spend a portion of that income (based on their MPC). This creates successive rounds of spending, leading to a total increase in national income that is larger than the initial injection.

questions.question: Write down the formula for the multiplier (k) using the Marginal Propensity to Consume, and briefly explain what MPC is.
questions.expected_answer: k = 1 / (1 - MPC). The Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is the proportion of any additional income that households spend on consumption.

questions.question: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.2, calculate the multiplier and explain what that specific number means for a R1 injection.
questions.expected_answer: k = 1 / MPS. So k = 1 / 0.2 = 5. A multiplier of 5 means that an initial injection of R1 will generate a total increase in national income of R5.
